Add simulation time settings and a zero-dependency Web-based UI alongside the terminal UI

impact_assessment.why: User requested time settings and a companion Web-based UI while keeping the terminal UI.
impact_assessment.benefits: Gives users precise temporal control in both terminal and browser, with rich Canvas 2D interactive exploration and zero external dependencies.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing CLI must remain 100% backward compatible; dependency: strictly standard library only (http.server); concurrency: clean server shutdown; state: time-reversible leapfrog with negative dt.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Thorough argument validation, modular web.py, self-contained embedded web UI, and full automated test suite.

Web studio parity: honor initial scenario and CLI physics/time options, make custom scenario uploads usable, and close input-handling gaps

impact_assessment.why: The new web UI silently ignores 'web KEY' and every physics/time flag, and drag-and-drop validation registers nothing, so the loaded custom scenario cannot be fetched; the upload endpoint also writes a fixed temp file in the working directory and accepts unbounded bodies.
impact_assessment.benefits: Browser and terminal share one selection and physics contract; custom scenarios load end-to-end; request handling is safe and deterministic.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: default web behaviour must remain unchanged for callers of run_server; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: registry shared across threaded requests; state: no files left in the working tree.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Optional WebOptions with defaults, a locked per-server registry, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, bounded Content-Length, and regression tests for the old defaults and new flags.

checkpoints.description: Task 'orrery-v9-web-parity' completed successfully.
Add one-click launchers for the browser studio on Windows, macOS and Linux

impact_assessment.why: The web UI could only be started by typing python -m orrery web; the terminal animation already had double-click launchers, so the browser path was undiscoverable.
impact_assessment.benefits: Double-click access to the studio on all three platforms, with the same Python 3.10 detection and visible failure handling as the existing launchers.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no change to existing run.* launchers or CLI; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: none; state: new files only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Mirror the proven launcher structure, cover it with launcher tests including CRLF, and smoke-test the Windows launcher.
